lessons.title: Hello, World!
lessons.description: Use print() to output text and write comments
hints: Text must be inside quotation marks, e.g. print("Sam").
Each print() outputs on its own line.
Comments start with # and are ignored by Python.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.description: Store values in variables and explore Python's basic data types
hints: Strings need quotes; numbers and True/False do not.
A float needs a decimal point, e.g. 1.75.
Use print(type(name)) to see a variable's type.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and Operators
lessons.description: Use Python's arithmetic operators to perform calculations
hints: subtotal = price * quantity
20% is the same as multiplying by 0.2.
total = subtotal + vat

lessons.title: Working with Strings
lessons.description: Join, format, index and slice strings
hints: Join strings with +, and remember to add a space: first_name + " " + last_name
The first character of a string is at index 0, e.g. first_name[0].
In an f-string, put variables inside curly brackets: f"{full_name}"

lessons.title: User Input and Type Conversion
lessons.description: Ask the user for information and convert it to the right type
hints: input() always returns a string.
Wrap input() in int() to get a whole number: int(input("Year? "))
If 5 and 3 gives 53, you have joined two strings instead of adding two numbers.

lessons.title: Booleans and Comparisons
lessons.description: Compare values and combine conditions with and, or and not
hints: Use == to compare and = to assign.
can_enter = age >= 18 and has_ticket and not is_banned
and is only True if every part is True.

lessons.title: Making Decisions with if Statements
lessons.description: Use if, elif and else to choose what your program does
hints: Every if, elif and else line ends with a colon.
Indent the code inside each block by four spaces.
Check the highest boundary first: if mark >= 70, then elif mark >= 60, and so on.

lessons.title: While Loops
lessons.description: Repeat code while a condition is True
hints: Start the countdown at 10 and use while count >= 1.
Subtract 1 each time with count -= 1, or the loop will never end.
Create attempts = 0 before the loop and add 1 inside it.

lessons.title: For Loops and range()
lessons.description: Repeat code a set number of times using for loops
hints: range(1, 13) gives the numbers 1 to 12.
Convert the input to a number with int() before multiplying.
Use an f-string for the format: f"{number} x {i} = {number * i}"

lessons.title: Lists
lessons.description: Store and work with collections of values
hints: max(marks) and min(marks) give the highest and lowest values.
The average is sum(marks) / len(marks).
Use marks.append(77) and then marks.sort().

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.description: Write reusable functions with parameters and return values
hints: Replace pass with a return statement, e.g. return width * height.
You can have several return statements in one function, one in each if/elif/else branch.
If your test prints None, the function is not returning anything yet.

lessons.title: Putting It Together: Number Guessing Game
lessons.description: Combine everything from this unit to build a number guessing game
hints: Use while guess != secret: as your loop condition.
Inside the loop: get the guess with int(input(...)), then add 1 to attempts.
Compare with if guess > secret: and elif guess < secret:
